themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best illustrates continuity from 1750 to 1900?
choices: Most of the world's people still worked in agriculture
New nations formed in Latin America after independence
Railroads crossed every inhabited continent by 1900
questions.explanation: Agriculture remained the main occupation worldwide.
choiceExplanations: Agriculture remained the main occupation worldwide.
Mechanized textile production was new after 1750, so it is a change.
New Latin American nations formed after 1810, which is a change.
Railroads were built only after 1830, which is a change.
questions.distinguisher: Mechanized textiles are a change, not a continuity.

questions.prompt: Which claim about the period 1750 to 1900 is most defensible?
choices: Political rights expanded equally for everyone
Political rights shrank everywhere as monarchs regained power
Political rights expanded only in Asia, especially in Meiji Japan
Political rights expanded for some groups while many remained excluded
questions.explanation: Some men gained votes while women and colonized peoples were excluded.
choiceExplanations: Expansion was concentrated in Europe and the Americas.
Some men gained votes while women and colonized peoples were excluded.
questions.distinguisher: Rights did not expand equally; women and colonized peoples were often excluded.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does the passage present as a continuity?
questions.explanation: The passage says most people still farmed.
choiceExplanations: The passage says most people still farmed.
The passage lists the formation of new nations among the changes.
The passage says machines transformed production, a change.
The spread of natural rights ideas is described as new.
questions.distinguisher: The formation of new nations is described as a change.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 5.10 key concept: continuity and change in political ideas, economies, and societies during the age of revolutions and industrialization
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing continuity and change, 1750–1900
stimulusBlocks.text:
Between 1750 and 1900, ideas of natural rights and national self-government spread widely, and new nations formed across the Americas and Europe. Machines and fossil fuels transformed how goods were made and moved.

Yet much continued. Most people in the world still farmed, monarchies still ruled many states, and the new industrial wealth was concentrated in a few countries. Political rights expanded for some groups while women, colonized peoples, and many workers remained excluded.

questions.prompt: The author would most likely agree that political change from 1750 to 1900 was
choices: significant but limited to some groups
complete and equal for all people, including women and colonized peoples
questions.explanation: Rights expanded for some while others remained excluded.
choiceExplanations: New nations formed in the Americas.
Rights expanded for some while others remained excluded.
questions.distinguisher: The author says women, colonized peoples, and many workers were excluded.
